metadata.title: A decade of educational research with the German National Educational Panel Study: A systematic review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This publication is a systematic review of peer-reviewed empirical studies using NEPS scientific use files, not an analysis of student microdata. Therefore, there is no analytic student sample for which survey weights (e.g., student design weights or replicate weights) would be applied. The review’s quantitative component relies on bibliometric counts and topic modeling of article text (titles/abstracts/keywords), so weighting variables from NEPS are not relevant to the reported results. For replication or extension using NEPS microdata, analysts would need to apply NEPS complex survey design weights and appropriate replicate-weight procedures as specified in the NEPS documentation for the relevant cohorts and waves.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this is a bibliometric/systematic review that does not estimate student-level cognitive achievement scores from NEPS (or any other ILSA) plausible values. The study’s outcomes are counts of publications, bibliometric impact indicators (e.g., FWCI), and topic-modeling metrics derived from article text, not PV-based achievement measures. Missing-data handling for PVs is therefore not part of the review’s methodology.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The review constructed a bibliometric database from the NEPS bibliography and augmented it with OpenAlex and Scopus searches. Inclusion required: (a) an empirical analysis using NEPS scientific use files (excluding conceptual descriptions and unpublished pilot-study data), (b) peer-reviewed journal publication (excluding gray literature and non-peer-reviewed items), (c) publication no later than 2024 (excluding advance online without final record), and (d) retrievable full text. The final corpus comprised 625 peer-reviewed articles meeting these criteria after deduplication and full-text screening.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICCS the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This systematic review synthesizes how NEPS data have been used in empirical educational research between 2013 and 2024, rather than estimating effects on student outcomes. The authors built a comprehensive bibliometric database (initially 1492 records, reduced to 625 eligible peer-reviewed articles) using NEPS bibliography plus OpenAlex and Scopus searches, applying strict inclusion/exclusion criteria (empirical NEPS use, peer-reviewed journal, full text available, and publication up to 2024). The review’s main quantitative outputs are publication counts, journal prestige/impact indicators (JIF quartiles and FWCI), and topic-modeling results using BERTopic with transformer-based embeddings (SPECTER 2), dimensionality reduction (UMAP), clustering (HDBSCAN), and TF-IDF-based topic terms. Because no student-level predictive modeling is performed, there are no ML performance metrics, PV handling, or missing-data strategies for achievement scores. Limitations include reliance on text-based topic modeling (inherently exploratory) and exclusion of gray literature and non-peer-reviewed outputs, which may underrepresent certain research themes. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a systematic review/bibliometric synthesis without an original student-level analytic dataset. Consequently, fields required for empirical ML on ILSA/NEPS microdata (e.g., total_students, country-level student counts, PV handling, missing-data handling for achievement scores, and ML model performance) are not applicable. The only methodological ML-like component is topic modeling for text analysis of abstracts/keywords, which is not a supervised predictive study of student outcomes and therefore does not populate the schema’s ML prediction fields.
